To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CpW(CO)(CH3)3 is a DNA-cleaving agent, that this cleavage is mediated by a methyl radical generated via photolysis of the metal-methyl bond, and that the cleavage is inhibited by TEMPO and cysteine.
CpW(CO)(3)-methyl radical, generated from CpW(CO)((3))CH(3) by irradiation, cleaves DNA by hydrogen atom abstraction, and this process is inhibited by the radical trap TEMPO.
the CpW(CO)(3)CH3 (1) complex undergoes photodecomposition, generating a carbon radical that cleaves DNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterization of organometallic compounds with a view to developing novel methods for the modification of DNA.
the design, synthesis, and characterization of new organometallic compounds that are active against DNA, and the elucidation of the mechanism of DNA cleavage.

the development of new methods for the synthesis of organic compounds, the development of new reagents that can cleave DNA, the development of novel methods for the synthesis and characterization of organometallic compounds, and the development of methods for the synthesis, characterization, and study of metal-alkyl compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the reaction is a single electron transfer (SET) reaction from the DNA to CpW(CO)(3)CH(3), and that the resulting W(CO)(3)(CH(2)) radical is the actual species responsible for the cleavage of the DNA.
the CpW(CO)(3)CH3 is an organic photoredox agent, not a metal-based one.
the reaction of 1.5 molecules of 1 with pBR322 DNA in the presence of 0.1 M cysteine and 0.5 mM TEMPO in aqueous solution at 25 degrees C for 1 h results in 100% single-strand scission of the DNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that a CpW(CO)(3)CH(3) molecule is capable of generating a methyl radical, and that this methyl radical is capable of abstracting hydrogen from a DNA base, thus cleaving a DNA strand.
we have shown that CpW(CO)(3)CH3 (1) and CpW(CO),(CH2)2CH3 (2) can cleave pBR322 DNA at 254 nm and that this cleavage is inhibited by TEMPO, cysteine and the metal chelating agent EDTA.
the first organometallic DNA-cleaving agent has been discovered and that it operates by the generation of a methyl radical from CpW(CO)(CH3)3.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of CpW(Co)3(CH3) to cleave DNA is not a viable approach for DNA sequencing or other applications.
Cp-metal complexes can be used to generate carbon radicals for DNA cleavage.
the metal-alkyl bonds in organometallic complexes can undergo homolysis upon irradiation, generating carbon-centered radicals that are capable of cleaving DNA.
